newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heat ends up on tighter supplies in US Gulf.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heat ends up on tighter supplies in US Gulf.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil rose sharply Monday on tighter distillate supply in the U.S. Gulf, prompting a bout of late session short covering in crude and gasoline, which reversed earlier losses, traders said.
"There is some distillate tightness in the (U.S.) Gulf that took everyone by surprise before the fourth cycle (shipping deadline), and that was the market's story," said a trader.
March heating oil settled up 1.23 cents at 61.76 cents a gallon. March crude ended up 23 cents at $22.46 a barrel while March gasoline finished up 0.47 cent a gallon at 63.53 cents.
"I expect crude's open interest to come in a bit," said a dealer, noting short covering in crude on healthy volume.
March crude fell as much as 58 cents early session to $21.65, spot crude's lowest level since August.

Cash traders said there was tighter heating oil supply in Texas as refiners have shifted their output away from distillate to gasoline ahead of the summer driving season. Meanwhile, traders needed to reserve space on the Colonial Pipeline for to meet a distillate shipping deadline.
"There was kind of a squeeze," said a futures dealer. Much of heating oil's strength was in the prompt month.

Monday's positive settlement in the oil complex snapped a four session streak of declines which had stripped almost $2.00 a barrel off of crude's price. Still, dealers said the bearish direction of the market remains intact as it is fueled by seasonal factors depressing refined product demand.

March crude's settlement Monday is the lowest spot crude close since August. But, chartists said spot crude's low Monday of 21.65 held support of around 21.70 established by March crude's session low November 6.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
